title: Glass Box
tagline: How modern AI works, in three acts — a real transformer trained live in the browser
hub_blurb: Train a small transformer live, compare direct and reasoned answers, then steer a tool-using agent and test its memory.
card_blurb: Watch a real transformer train from scratch in your browser — gibberish to words to sentences — and tap its attention maps. Then see chain-of-thought beat direct answers in a fair fight, buy accuracy with thinking time, and drive a tool-using agent yourself — then break it by shrinking its memory.
description: **Glass Box** — how modern AI works, in three acts, for educators. Act 1 trains a real 42,458-parameter transformer from scratch in the browser — live loss curve, frozen era checkpoints (gibberish → words → sentences), real attention heatmaps you can tap, weight-matrix inspection, a temperature playground. Act 2 builds a reasoning model: two same-size brains trained with and without chain-of-thought on the same problems (54% vs 96% on the shipped run), an answer-key-free verifier that buys accuracy with test-time compute (60→78% from 1 to 8 attempts), and STaR-style self-improvement rounds where the model trains on its own certified work (49→85%). Act 3 is an agent: a real tool loop — genuine calculator errors and recovery, genuine document search, a context meter — where you can play the model yourself, and shrinking the context window genuinely breaks it. The engine computes its own transcendentals so seeded runs reproduce bit-for-bit on every device. Includes a printable presenter guide.
